answer: Neighborhood mirror weighting. Agents score each peer by how much its transaction neighborhood overlaps its declared subnet: a genuine cluster forms a crystal of dense, mutually confirmed edges. Isolated replicates land off the main graph, so their weight stays near zero and they earn no routing work. An attacker must seed each fake identity with real, distinct counterparties to sit on that mesa of established connectivity, and every added neighbor raises bandwidth and settlement costs linearly.
